caption: The drawing consists of several outlined geometric shapes, each marked with capital letters (A, B, B1, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, W) and additional labels for orientation and assembly. The largest shapes, labeled A and A-2, are rectangular with “CENTER BACK” and “CENTER FRONT” written along their longer edges, and both marked “CUT ON FOLD.” Another large shape, B, is an irregular curved piece, and B1 is a smaller, similarly curved piece, both with small triangle marks on the edges. The shape labeled C is a rectangle referencing the collar, also noted as "CUT ON FOLD." D and E are additional rectangles, E being smaller, with small diagonal hatching along one edge. The shapes F and H are triangles or wedges, with one edge marked with a dotted line. G is a long, thin rectangle; I is a small rectangle. W is a square, and S is a small triangular piece. The layout is rendered in graphite or black ink on a cream-colored background, with all annotations in capital letters. An explanatory block of text in the lower right provides instructions for sewing and assembly, referring to the labeled pieces. The overall composition is organized, with the components evenly arranged to fit within a rectangular boundary, typical of sewing patterns or garment construction diagrams.
title: Pattern for Man's Shirt
